svg.text: 43 nodes · 216 relationships · 37 implied labels, generated from the OASIS STIX 2.1 JSON schemas, the STIX validator 3.3.2 relationship table and the STIX 2.1 specification. The main arrows are named by their relationship type; hover any arrow for its name and description, and cards link to the object's section of the specification.
subtype: also carries the supertype's label

path.title: CONTAINS_REFS: Specifies a list of references to other File and/or Directory Objects contained within the directory. The contains_refs property of a Directory, a list of identifiers of Directory, File objects.

CONTAINS_REFS: Specifies a list of references to other File and/or Directory Objects contained within the directory. The contains_refs property of a Directory, a list of identifiers of Directory, File objects.

RESOLVES_TO_REFS: Specifies a list of references to one or more IP addresses or domain names that the domain name resolves to. The resolves_to_refs property of a DomainName, a list of identifiers of DomainName, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr objects.

RESOLVES_TO: This Relationship describes that this Domain Name resolves to one or more IP addresses or domain names. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'resolves-to', source_ref a DomainName and target_ref a DomainName.

RESOLVES_TO_REFS: Specifies a list of references to one or more IP addresses or domain names that the domain name resolves to. The resolves_to_refs property of a DomainName, a list of identifiers of DomainName, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr objects.

RESOLVES_TO: This Relationship describes that this Domain Name resolves to one or more IP addresses or domain names. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'resolves-to', source_ref a DomainName and target_ref an Ipv4Addr.

RESOLVES_TO_REFS: Specifies a list of references to one or more IP addresses or domain names that the domain name resolves to. The resolves_to_refs property of a DomainName, a list of identifiers of DomainName, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr objects.

BELONGS_TO_REF: Specifies the user account that the email address belongs to, as a reference to a User Account Object. The belongs_to_ref property of an EmailAddr, an identifier of a UserAccount.
FROM_REF: Specifies the value of the 'From:' header of the email message. The from_ref property of an EmailMessage, an identifier of an EmailAddr.
SENDER_REF: Specifies the value of the 'From' field of the email message. The sender_ref property of an EmailMessage, an identifier of an EmailAddr.
TO_REFS: Specifies the mailboxes that are 'To:' recipients of the email message. The to_refs property of an EmailMessage, a list of identifiers of an EmailAddr.
CC_REFS: Specifies the mailboxes that are 'CC:' recipients of the email message. The cc_refs property of an EmailMessage, a list of identifiers of an EmailAddr.
BCC_REFS: Specifies the mailboxes that are 'BCC:' recipients of the email message. The bcc_refs property of an EmailMessage, a list of identifiers of an EmailAddr.

RAW_EMAIL_REF: Specifies the raw binary contents of the email message, including both the headers and body, as a reference to an Artifact Object. The raw_email_ref property of an EmailMessage, an identifier of an Artifact.

BODY_RAW_REF: Specifies the contents of non-textual MIME parts, that is those whose content_type does not start with text/, as a reference to an Artifact Object or File Object. The body_raw_ref property of the body_multipart entries of an EmailMessage, an identifier of an Artifact.

BODY_RAW_REF: Specifies the contents of non-textual MIME parts, that is those whose content_type does not start with text/, as a reference to an Artifact Object or File Object. The body_raw_ref property of the body_multipart entries of an EmailMessage, an identifier of a File.
CREATED_BY_REF: The ID of the Source object that describes who created this object. The created_by_ref property of an ExtensionDefinition, an identifier of an Identity.
OBJECT_MARKING_REFS: The list of marking-definition objects to be applied to this object. The object_marking_refs property of an ExtensionDefinition, a list of identifiers of a MarkingDefinition.
PARENT_DIRECTORY_REF: Specifies the parent directory of the file, as a reference to a Directory Object. The parent_directory_ref property of a File, an identifier of a Directory.
CONTAINS_REFS: Specifies a list of references to other Observable Objects contained within the file. The contains_refs property of a File, a list of identifiers of a StixCyberObservableObject.
CONTENT_REF: Specifies the content of the file, represented as an Artifact Object. The content_ref property of a File, an identifier of an Artifact.

CONTAINS_REFS: Specifies the files contained in the archive, as a reference to one or more other File Objects. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type file-object. The contains_refs property of the archive-ext extension of a File, a list of identifiers of a File.

OBJECT_REFS: The STIX Objects (SDOs and SROs) that are referred to by this Grouping. The object_refs property of a Grouping, a list of identifiers of StixCyberObservableObject, StixDomainObject, Sighting objects. Required. It may also name STIX relationship objects, which the graph holds as relationships, not nodes.

RESOLVES_TO_REFS: Specifies a list of references to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses that the IPv4 address resolves to. The resolves_to_refs property of an Ipv4Addr, a list of identifiers of a MacAddr.

RESOLVES_TO: This Relationship describes that this IPv4 Address resolves to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'resolves-to', source_ref an Ipv4Addr and target_ref a MacAddr.

BELONGS_TO_REFS: Specifies a reference to one or more autonomous systems (AS) that the IPv4 address belongs to. The belongs_to_refs property of an Ipv4Addr, a list of identifiers of an AutonomousSystem.

BELONGS_TO: This Relationship describes that this IPv4 Address belongs to one or more autonomous systems (AS). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'belongs-to', source_ref an Ipv4Addr and target_ref an AutonomousSystem.

RESOLVES_TO_REFS: Specifies a list of references to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses that the IPv6 address resolves to. The resolves_to_refs property of an Ipv6Addr, a list of identifiers of a MacAddr.

OPERATING_SYSTEM_REFS: The operating systems that the malware family or malware instance is executable on. The operating_system_refs property of a Malware, a list of identifiers of a Software.

SAMPLE_REFS: The sample_refs property specifies a list of identifiers of the SCO file or artifact objects associated with this malware instance(s) or family. The sample_refs property of a Malware, a list of identifiers of Artifact, File objects.

SAMPLE_REFS: The sample_refs property specifies a list of identifiers of the SCO file or artifact objects associated with this malware instance(s) or family. The sample_refs property of a Malware, a list of identifiers of Artifact, File objects.

DOWNLOADS: These Relationships document that this malware instance (or family) downloads or drops another malware instance, tool or file. This is especially common with "first-stage" malware instances such as downloaders and droppers. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'downloads', source_ref a Malware and target_ref a File.

DROPS: These Relationships document that this malware instance (or family) downloads or drops another malware instance, tool or file. This is especially common with "first-stage" malware instances such as downloaders and droppers. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'drops', source_ref a Malware and target_ref a File.

HOST_VM_REF: A description of the virtual machine environment used to host the guest operating system (if applicable) that was used for the dynamic analysis of the malware instance or family. The host_vm_ref property of a MalwareAnalysis, an identifier of a Software.
OPERATING_SYSTEM_REF: The operating system that was used to perform the dynamic analysis. The operating_system_ref property of a MalwareAnalysis, an identifier of a Software.

INSTALLED_SOFTWARE_REFS: Any non-standard software installed on the operating system used for the dynamic analysis of the malware instance or family. The installed_software_refs property of a MalwareAnalysis, a list of identifiers of a Software.
ANALYSIS_SCO_REFS: The list of STIX objects that were captured during the analysis process. The analysis_sco_refs property of a MalwareAnalysis, a list of identifiers of a StixCyberObservableObject.
SAMPLE_REF: Refers to the object this analysis was performed against. The sample_ref property of a MalwareAnalysis, an identifier of Artifact, File, NetworkTraffic objects.
SAMPLE_REF: Refers to the object this analysis was performed against. The sample_ref property of a MalwareAnalysis, an identifier of Artifact, File, NetworkTraffic objects.
SAMPLE_REF: Refers to the object this analysis was performed against. The sample_ref property of a MalwareAnalysis, an identifier of Artifact, File, NetworkTraffic objects.

CREATED_BY_REF: The created_by_ref property specifies the ID of the identity object that describes the entity that created this Marking Definition. The created_by_ref property of a MarkingDefinition, an identifier of an Identity.

OBJECT_MARKING_REFS: The object_marking_refs property specifies a list of IDs of marking-definition objects that apply to this Marking Definition. The object_marking_refs property of a MarkingDefinition, a list of identifiers of a MarkingDefinition.

SRC_REF: Specifies the source of the network traffic, as a reference to an Observable Object. The src_ref property of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of DomainName, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, MacAddr objects.

DST_REF: Specifies the destination of the network traffic, as a reference to an Observable Object. The dst_ref property of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of DomainName, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, MacAddr objects.

DST_REF: Specifies the destination of the network traffic, as a reference to an Observable Object. The dst_ref property of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of DomainName, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, MacAddr objects.
SRC_PAYLOAD_REF: Specifies the bytes sent from the source to the destination. The src_payload_ref property of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of an Artifact.
DST_PAYLOAD_REF: Specifies the bytes sent from the source to the destination. The dst_payload_ref property of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of an Artifact.

MESSAGE_BODY_DATA_REF: Specifies the data contained in the HTTP message body, if included. The message_body_data_ref property of the http-request-ext extension of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of an Artifact.
ENCAPSULATES_REFS: Links to other network-traffic objects encapsulated by a network-traffic. The encapsulates_refs property of a NetworkTraffic, a list of identifiers of a NetworkTraffic.
ENCAPSULATED_BY_REF: Links to another network-traffic object which encapsulates this object. The encapsulated_by_ref property of a NetworkTraffic, an identifier of a NetworkTraffic.

OBJECT_REFS: The STIX Objects (SDOs and SROs) that the note is being applied to. The object_refs property of a Note, a list of identifiers of StixCyberObservableObject, StixDomainObject, Sighting objects. Required. It may also name STIX relationship objects, which the graph holds as relationships, not nodes.

OPENED_CONNECTION_REFS: Specifies the list of network connections opened by the process, as a reference to one or more Network Traffic Objects. The opened_connection_refs property of a Process, a list of identifiers of a NetworkTraffic.
CREATOR_USER_REF: Specifies the user that created the process, as a reference to a User Account Object. The creator_user_ref property of a Process, an identifier of a UserAccount.
IMAGE_REF: Specifies the executable binary that was executed as the process image, as a reference to a File Object. The image_ref property of a Process, an identifier of a File.

SERVICE_DLL_REFS: Specifies the DLLs loaded by the service, as a reference to one or more File Objects. The service_dll_refs property of the windows-service-ext extension of a Process, a list of identifiers of a File.
PARENT_REF: Specifies the other process that spawned (i.e. is the parent of) this one, as represented by a Process Object. The parent_ref property of a Process, an identifier of a Process.

CHILD_REFS: Specifies the other processes that were spawned by (i.e. children of) this process, as a reference to one or more other Process Objects. The child_refs property of a Process, a list of identifiers of a Process.

OBJECT_REFS: Specifies the STIX Objects that are referred to by this Report. The object_refs property of a Report, a list of identifiers of StixCyberObservableObject, StixDomainObject, Sighting objects. Required. It may also name STIX relationship objects, which the graph holds as relationships, not nodes.

WHERE_SIGHTED_REFS: A list of ID references to the Identity or Location objects describing the entities or types of entities that saw the sighting. The where_sighted_refs property of a Sighting, a list of identifiers of Identity, Location objects.
OBJECT_MARKING_REFS: The list of marking-definition objects to be applied to this object. The object_marking_refs property of a Sighting, a list of identifiers of a MarkingDefinition.
SIGHTING_OF_REF: An ID reference to the object that has been sighted. The sighting_of_ref property of a Sighting, an identifier of a StixDomainObject. Required.

OBSERVED_DATA_REFS: A list of ID references to the Observed Data objects that contain the raw cyber data for this Sighting. The observed_data_refs property of a Sighting, a list of identifiers of an ObservedData.

WHERE_SIGHTED_REFS: A list of ID references to the Identity or Location objects describing the entities or types of entities that saw the sighting. The where_sighted_refs property of a Sighting, a list of identifiers of Identity, Location objects.

CREATOR_USER_REF: Specifies a reference to a user account, represented as a User Account Object, that created the registry key. The creator_user_ref property of a WindowsRegistryKey, an identifier of a UserAccount.
CREATED_BY_REF: The ID of the Source object that describes who created this object. The created_by_ref property of every SDO, an identifier of an Identity.
OBJECT_MARKING_REFS: The list of marking-definition objects to be applied to this object. The object_marking_refs property of every SDO, a list of identifiers of a MarkingDefinition.
OBJECT_MARKING_REFS: The list of marking-definition objects to be applied to this object. The object_marking_refs property of every SCO, a list of identifiers of a MarkingDefinition.

DELIVERS: This Relationship describes that this Attack Pattern is used to deliver this malware instance (or family). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'delivers', source_ref an AttackPattern and target_ref a Malware.

USES: This Relationship describes that the related Malware or Tool is used to perform the behavior identified in the Attack Pattern. For example, a uses Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for a distributed denial of service (DDoS) to a Tool for Low Orbit Ion Cannon (LOIC) indicates that the tool can be used to perform those DDoS attacks. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref an AttackPattern and target_ref a Malware.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that this Attack Pattern typically targets the type of victim, location, or vulnerability represented by the related Identity, Location, or Vulnerability object. For example, a targets Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to an Identity object representing domain administrators means that the form of SQL injection characterized by the Attack Pattern targets domain administrators in order to achieve its objectives. Another example is a Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to a Vulnerability in blogging software means that the particular SQL injection attack exploits that vulnerability. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref an AttackPattern and target_ref an Identity.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that this Attack Pattern typically targets the type of victim, location, or vulnerability represented by the related Identity, Location, or Vulnerability object. For example, a targets Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to an Identity object representing domain administrators means that the form of SQL injection characterized by the Attack Pattern targets domain administrators in order to achieve its objectives. Another example is a Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to a Vulnerability in blogging software means that the particular SQL injection attack exploits that vulnerability. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref an AttackPattern and target_ref a Location.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that this Attack Pattern typically targets the type of victim, location, or vulnerability represented by the related Identity, Location, or Vulnerability object. For example, a targets Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to an Identity object representing domain administrators means that the form of SQL injection characterized by the Attack Pattern targets domain administrators in order to achieve its objectives. Another example is a Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to a Vulnerability in blogging software means that the particular SQL injection attack exploits that vulnerability. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref an AttackPattern and target_ref a Vulnerability.

USES: This Relationship describes that the related Malware or Tool is used to perform the behavior identified in the Attack Pattern. For example, a uses Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for a distributed denial of service (DDoS) to a Tool for Low Orbit Ion Cannon (LOIC) indicates that the tool can be used to perform those DDoS attacks. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref an AttackPattern and target_ref a Tool.

ATTRIBUTED_TO: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set or Threat Actor that is involved in carrying out the Campaign. For example, an attributed-to Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to the Urban Fowl Threat Actor means that the actor carried out or was involved in some of the activity described by the Campaign. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'attributed-to', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref an IntrusionSet.

ATTRIBUTED_TO: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set or Threat Actor that is involved in carrying out the Campaign. For example, an attributed-to Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to the Urban Fowl Threat Actor means that the actor carried out or was involved in some of the activity described by the Campaign. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'attributed-to', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref a ThreatActor.

COMPROMISES: This Relationship describes that the Campaign compromises the related Infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'compromises', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref an Infrastructure.

USES: This Relationship describes that attacks carried out as part of the Campaign typically use the related Attack Pattern, Infrastructure, Malware, or Tool. For example, a uses Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used during attacks attributed to that Campaign. A campaign, threat actor, intrusion set, malware, or tool takes infrastructure and compromises and/or uses it for their own. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref an Infrastructure.

ORIGINATES_FROM: This Relationship describes that the Campaign originates from the related Location. For example, an originates-from relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to a Location representing North America means that Glass Gazelle appears to originate from or is located in North America. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'originates-from', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref a Location.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that the Campaign uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed as part of Glass Gazelle often exploit that Vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to an Identity describing the energy sector in the United States means that the Campaign typically carries out attacks against targets in that sector. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref a Location.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that the Campaign uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed as part of Glass Gazelle often exploit that Vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to an Identity describing the energy sector in the United States means that the Campaign typically carries out attacks against targets in that sector. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref an Identity.

Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref a Vulnerability.

A campaign, threat actor, intrusion set, malware, or tool takes infrastructure and compromises and/or uses it for their own. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref a Campaign and target_ref an AttackPattern.

INVESTIGATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can be used to investigate the Indicator. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'investigates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref an Indicator.

MITIGATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can mitigate (e.g. respond to a threat) the related Attack Pattern, Indicator, Malware, Vulnerability, or Tool. For example, a mitigates Relationship from a Course of Action object to a Malware object indicates that the course of action mitigates the malware. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'mitigates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref an Indicator.
MITIGATES: See forward relationship for definition. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'mitigates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref an AttackPattern.

MITIGATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can mitigate (e.g. respond to a threat) the related Attack Pattern, Indicator, Malware, Vulnerability, or Tool. For example, a mitigates Relationship from a Course of Action object to a Malware object indicates that the course of action mitigates the malware. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'mitigates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref a Malware.

REMEDIATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can be used to remediate (e.g. clean up) the malware or vulnerability. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'remediates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref a Malware.

MITIGATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can mitigate (e.g. respond to a threat) the related Attack Pattern, Indicator, Malware, Vulnerability, or Tool. For example, a mitigates Relationship from a Course of Action object to a Malware object indicates that the course of action mitigates the malware. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'mitigates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref a Tool.

MITIGATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can mitigate (e.g. respond to a threat) the related Attack Pattern, Indicator, Malware, Vulnerability, or Tool. For example, a mitigates Relationship from a Course of Action object to a Malware object indicates that the course of action mitigates the malware. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'mitigates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref a Vulnerability.

REMEDIATES: This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can be used to remediate (e.g. clean up) the malware or vulnerability. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'remediates', source_ref a CourseOfAction and target_ref a Vulnerability.

LOCATED_AT: This Relationship describes that the Identity is located at or in the related Location. For example, a located-at relationship from the ACME Corporation to a Location representing the United States means that ACME Corporation is located in the United States. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'located-at', source_ref an Identity and target_ref a Location.

BASED_ON: This relationship describes that the indicator was created based on information from an observed-data object. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'based-on', source_ref an Indicator and target_ref an ObservedData.

INDICATES: See forward relationship for definition. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'indicates', source_ref an Indicator and target_ref a Campaign.

INDICATES: This Relationship describes that the Indicator can detect evidence of the related Attack Pattern, Campaign, Infrastructure, Intrusion Set, Malware, Threat Actor, or Tool. This evidence may not be direct: for example, the Indicator may detect secondary evidence of the Campaign, such as malware or behavior commonly used by that Campaign. For example, an indicates Relationship from an Indicator to a Campaign object representing Glass Gazelle means that the Indicator is capable of detecting evidence of Glass Gazelle, such as command and control IPs commonly used by that Campaign. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'indicates', source_ref an Indicator and target_ref an Infrastructure.

COMMUNICATES_WITH: This Relationship documents that this infrastructure instance communicates with the defined network addressable resource. For example, a botnet could communicate with a crypto-currency mining pool. This does not mean that the pool is a part of this infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'communicates-with', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a DomainName.

For example, a botnet could communicate with a crypto-currency mining pool. This does not mean that the pool is a part of this infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'communicates-with', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref an Infrastructure.

CONSISTS_OF: This Relationship documents the objects that are used to make up an infrastructure instance, such as ipv4-addr, ipv6-addr, domain-name, url. An infrastructure instance consists of zero or more objects. While not all SCO types will make sense as infrastructure, allowing any type of SCO prevents artificially restricting what could be used. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'consists-of', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref an Infrastructure.

CONTROLS: This Relationship describes that this infrastructure controls some other infrastructure or a malware instance (or family). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'controls', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref an Infrastructure.

USES: This Relationship describes that this infrastructure uses this other infrastructure to achieve its objectives. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref an Infrastructure.

CONTROLS: This Relationship describes that this infrastructure controls some other infrastructure or a malware instance (or family). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'controls', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a Malware.

DELIVERS: This Relationship describes that this infrastructure is used to actively deliver a malware instance (or family). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'delivers', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a Malware.

HOSTS: This Relationship describes that this infrastructure has a tool running on it or is used to passively host the tool / malware. For example, an SSH server may be hosted on a piece of infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'hosts', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a Malware.

HAS: This Relationship describes that this specific Infrastructure has this specific Vulnerability. For example, a web server may not have been patched and currently is impacted by a CVE. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'has', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a Vulnerability.

HOSTS: This Relationship describes that this infrastructure has a tool running on it or is used to passively host the tool / malware. For example, an SSH server may be hosted on a piece of infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'hosts', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a Tool.

LOCATED_AT: This Relationship describes that the infrastructure originates from the related location. For example, a located-at relationship from the Red Orca C2 infrastructure to a Location representing North America means that the Red Orca C2 Infrastructure appears to originate from or is located in North America. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'located-at', source_ref an Infrastructure and target_ref a Location.

ATTRIBUTED_TO: This Relationship describes that the related Threat Actor is involved in carrying out the Intrusion Set. For example, an attributed-to Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to the Urban Fowl Threat Actor means that the actor carried out or was involved in some of the activity described by the Intrusion Set. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'attributed-to', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref a ThreatActor.

COMPROMISES: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set compromises the related Infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'compromises', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref an Infrastructure.

HOSTS: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set hosts or owns the related Infrastructure (e.g. an actor that rents botnets to other threat actors). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'hosts', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref an Infrastructure.

OWNS: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set hosts or owns the related Infrastructure (e.g. an actor that rents botnets to other threat actors). Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'owns', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref an Infrastructure.

USES: This Relationship describes that attacks carried out as part of the Intrusion Set typically use the related Attack Pattern, Infrastructure, Malware, or Tool. For example, a uses Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used during attacks attributed to that Intrusion Set. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref an Infrastructure.

ORIGINATES_FROM: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set originates from the related location and SHOULD NOT be used to define attribution. For example, an originates-from relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to a Location representing North America means that the Red Orca Intrusion Set appears to originate from or is located in North America. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'originates-from', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref a Location.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed as part of Red Orca often exploit that Vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to an Identity describing the energy sector in the United States means that the Intrusion Set typically carries out attacks against targets in that sector. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref an IntrusionSet and target_ref a Location.

TARGETS: This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed as part of Red Orca often exploit that Vulnerability. CONTROLS: This Relationship documents that this malware instance (or family) can control other malware which may be resident on the same system on which it is executing. Note that this is not meant to imply or state that the malware instance or family drops other malware (which is covered by the drops relationship). Rather, it is meant to state that the malware instance or family is able to subvert or control other malware to achieve its goals. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'controls', source_ref a Malware and target_ref a Malware.

DOWNLOADS: These Relationships document that this malware instance (or family) downloads or drops another malware instance, tool or file. This is especially common with "first-stage" malware instances such as downloaders and droppers. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'downloads', source_ref a Malware and target_ref a Malware.

DROPS: These Relationships document that this malware instance (or family) downloads or drops another malware instance, tool or file. This is especially common with "first-stage" malware instances such as downloaders and droppers. For example, a uses Relationship from the jay-sm17h Threat Actor to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used by jay-sm17h. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref a Malware and target_ref a Malware.

VARIANT_OF: This Relationship is used to document that one malware instance or family is a variant of another malware instance or family. Only the following uses of this relationship are valid: Malware instance → Malware family: a Malware instance is a variant of a Malware family. For example, a particular Zeus version 2 sample is a variant of the broader Zeus family. Malware family → Malware family: a Malware family is a variant of another Malware family. For example, the Gameover Zeus family is a variant of the broader Zeus family. Malware instance → Malware instance: a Malware instance is a variant of another Malware instance. For example, a particular Cryptolocker instance that is based on an another Cryptolocker instance with minor changes. Malware family → Malware instance: this relationship MUST NOT be used as it is not semantically valid. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'variant-of', source_ref a Malware and target_ref a Malware.

DOWNLOADS: These Relationships document that this malware instance (or family) downloads or drops another malware instance, tool or file. DROPS: These Relationships document that this malware instance (or family) downloads or drops another malware instance, tool or file. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref a Tool and target_ref an Identity.

TARGETS: This Relationship documents that this Tool is being used to target this Identity, Infrastructure, Location, or exploit the Vulnerability. For example, a targets Relationship linking an exploit Tool to a Vulnerability for CVE-2016-0001 means that the tool exploits that vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship linking a DDoS Tool to an Identity representing the energy sector means that Tool is typically used against targets in the energy sector. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref a Tool and target_ref an Infrastructure.

USES: This Relationship describes that this Tool uses the related Infrastructure. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'uses', source_ref a Tool and target_ref an Infrastructure.

TARGETS: This Relationship documents that this Tool is being used to target this Identity, Infrastructure, Location, or exploit the Vulnerability. For example, a targets Relationship linking an exploit Tool to a Vulnerability for CVE-2016-0001 means that the tool exploits that vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship linking a DDoS Tool to an Identity representing the energy sector means that Tool is typically used against targets in the energy sector. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'targets', source_ref a Tool and target_ref a Location.

IMPACTS: Listed by the OASIS STIX validator; the STIX 2.1 specification doesn't define it. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'impacts', source_ref a Vulnerability and target_ref an Infrastructure.

IMPACTS: Listed by the OASIS STIX validator; the STIX 2.1 specification doesn't define it. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'impacts', source_ref a Vulnerability and target_ref a Tool.

DERIVED_FROM: The information in the target object is based on information from the source object. Both objects are of the same type. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'derived-from', source_ref a StixDomainObject and target_ref a StixDomainObject.

DUPLICATE_OF: The referenced source and target objects are semantically duplicates of each other. Both objects are of the same type. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'duplicate-of', source_ref a StixDomainObject and target_ref a StixDomainObject.

RELATED_TO: Asserts a non-specific relationship between two objects. Used when no other relationship type is suitable. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'related-to', source_ref a StixDomainObject and target_ref a StixDomainObject.

DERIVED_FROM: The information in the target object is based on information from the source object. Both objects are of the same type. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'derived-from', source_ref a StixCyberObservableObject and target_ref a StixCyberObservableObject.

DUPLICATE_OF: The referenced source and target objects are semantically duplicates of each other. Both objects are of the same type. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'duplicate-of', source_ref a StixCyberObservableObject and target_ref a StixCyberObservableObject.

RELATED_TO: Asserts a non-specific relationship between two objects. Used when no other relationship type is suitable. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'related-to', source_ref a StixCyberObservableObject and target_ref a StixCyberObservableObject.

RELATED_TO: Asserts a non-specific relationship between two objects. Used when no other relationship type is suitable. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'related-to', source_ref a StixDomainObject and target_ref a StixCyberObservableObject.

RELATED_TO: Asserts a non-specific relationship between two objects. Used when no other relationship type is suitable. Stored in STIX as a relationship object with relationship_type 'related-to', source_ref a StixCyberObservableObject and target_ref a StixDomainObject.

g.title: AttackPattern — Attack Patterns are a type of TTP that describe ways that adversaries attempt to compromise targets. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, aliases, name, description, kill_chain_phases

Campaign — A Campaign is a grouping of adversary behavior that describes a set of malicious activities or attacks that occur over a period of time against a specific set of targets. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, aliases, first_seen, last_seen, objective

CourseOfAction — A Course of Action is an action taken either to prevent an attack or to respond to an attack that is in progress. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description

Grouping — A Grouping object explicitly asserts that the referenced STIX Objects have a shared content. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, context

Identity — Identities can represent actual individuals, organizations, or groups (e.g., ACME, Inc.) as well as classes of individuals, organizations, or groups. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, roles, name, description, identity_class, sectors, contact_information

Incident — The Incident object in STIX 2.1 is a stub, to be expanded in future STIX 2 releases. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description

Indicator — Indicators contain a pattern that can be used to detect suspicious or malicious cyber activity. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, indicator_types, name, description, pattern, pattern_type, pattern_version, valid_from, valid_until, kill_chain_phases

Infrastructure — Infrastructure objects describe systems, software services, and associated physical or virtual resources. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, infrastructure_types, aliases, kill_chain_phases, first_seen, last_seen

IntrusionSet — An Intrusion Set is a grouped set of adversary behavior and resources with common properties that is believed to be orchestrated by a single organization. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, aliases, first_seen, last_seen, goals, resource_level, primary_motivation, secondary_motivations

Location — A Location represents a geographic location. The location may be described as any, some or all of the following: region (e.g., North America), civic address (e.g. New York, US), latitude and longitude. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, description, name, latitude, longitude, precision, region, country, administrative_area, city, street_address, postal_code

Malware — Malware is a type of TTP that is also known as malicious code and malicious software, refers to a program that is inserted into a system, usually covertly, with the intent of compromising the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the victim's data, applications, or operating system (OS) or of otherwise annoying or disrupting the victim. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, aliases, first_seen, last_seen, architecture_execution_envs, implementation_languages, capabilities, malware_types, name, description, kill_chain_phases, is_family

MalwareAnalysis — Malware Analysis captures the metadata and results of a particular analysis performed (static or dynamic) on the malware instance or family. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, product, version, configuration_version, modules, analysis_engine_version, analysis_definition_version, submitted, analysis_started, analysis_ended, result_name, result

Note — A Note is a comment or note containing informative text to help explain the context of one or more STIX Objects (SDOs or SROs) or to provide additional analysis that is not contained in the original object. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, abstract, content, authors

ObservedData — Observed data conveys information that was observed on systems and networks, such as log data or network traffic, using the Cyber Observable specification. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, first_observed, last_observed, number_observed, objects

Opinion — An Opinion is an assessment of the correctness of the information in a STIX Object produced by a different entity and captures the level of agreement or disagreement using a fixed scale. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, explanation, authors, opinion

Report — Reports are collections of threat intelligence focused on one or more topics, such as a description of a threat actor, malware, or attack technique, including context and related details. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, report_types, name, description, published
StixDomainObject — Any STIX Domain Object (SDO): a higher-level intelligence object, such as an Attack Pattern, Malware or Threat Actor. Every SDO node also carries this label. Properties: id

ThreatActor — Threat Actors are actual individuals, groups, or organizations believed to be operating with malicious intent. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, threat_actor_types, name, description, aliases, roles, goals, first_seen, last_seen, sophistication, resource_level, primary_motivation, secondary_motivations, personal_motivations

Tool — Tools are legitimate software that can be used by threat actors to perform attacks. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, aliases, tool_types, name, description, tool_version, kill_chain_phases

Vulnerability — A Vulnerability is a mistake in software that can be directly used by a hacker to gain access to a system or network. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description

Artifact — The Artifact Object permits capturing an array of bytes (8-bits), as a base64-encoded string string, or linking to a file-like payload. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, mime_type, payload_bin, url, hashes, encryption_algorithm, decryption_key
AutonomousSystem — The AS object represents the properties of an Autonomous Systems (AS). Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, number, name, rir

Directory — The Directory Object represents the properties common to a file system directory. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, path, path_enc, ctime, mtime, atime
DomainName — The Domain Name represents the properties of a network domain name. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value
EmailAddr — The Email Address Object represents a single email address. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value, display_name

EmailMessage — The Email Message Object represents an instance of an email message. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, date, content_type, message_id, subject, received_lines, additional_header_fields, is_multipart, body, body_multipart

File — The File Object represents the properties of a file. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, hashes, size, name, name_enc, magic_number_hex, mime_type, ctime, mtime, atime
Ipv4Addr — The IPv4 Address Object represents one or more IPv4 addresses expressed using CIDR notation. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value
Ipv6Addr — The IPv6 Address Object represents one or more IPv6 addresses expressed using CIDR notation. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value
MacAddr — The MAC Address Object represents a single Media Access Control (MAC) address. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value
Mutex — The Mutex Object represents the properties of a mutual exclusion (mutex) object. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, name

NetworkTraffic — The Network Traffic Object represents arbitrary network traffic that originates from a source and is addressed to a destination. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, start, end, src_port, dst_port, protocols, src_byte_count, dst_byte_count, src_packets, dst_packets, ipfix, is_active

Process — The Process Object represents common properties of an instance of a computer program as executed on an operating system. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, is_hidden, pid, created_time, cwd, command_line, environment_variables

Software — The Software Object represents high-level properties associated with software, including software products. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, name, cpe, swid, languages, vendor, version

StixCyberObservableObject — Any STIX Cyber-observable Object (SCO): a fact observed on a system or network, such as a File, Process or IPv4 Address. Every SCO node also carries this label. Properties: id
Url — The URL Object represents the properties of a uniform resource locator (URL). Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value

UserAccount — The User Account Object represents an instance of any type of user account, including but not limited to operating system, device, messaging service, and social media platform accounts. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, user_id, credential, account_login, account_type, display_name, is_service_account, is_privileged, can_escalate_privs, is_disabled, account_created, account_expires, credential_last_changed, account_first_login, account_last_login

WindowsRegistryKey — The Registry Key Object represents the properties of a Windows registry key. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, key, values, modified_time, number_of_subkeys

X509Certificate — The X509 Certificate Object represents the properties of an X.509 certificate. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, is_self_signed, hashes, version, serial_number, signature_algorithm, issuer, validity_not_before, validity_not_after, subject, subject_public_key_algorithm, subject_public_key_modulus, subject_public_key_exponent, x509_v3_extensions

Sighting — A Sighting denotes the belief that something in CTI (e.g., an indicator, malware, tool, threat actor, etc.) was seen. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, description, first_seen, last_seen, count, summary

ExtensionDefinition — The STIX Extension Definition object allows producers of threat intelligence to extend existing STIX objects or to create entirely new STIX objects in a standardized way. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, schema, version, extension_types, extension_properties

LanguageContent — The language-content object represents text content for STIX Objects represented in languages other than that of the original object. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, object_modified, contents

MarkingDefinition — The marking-definition object represents a specific marking. Properties: id, type, spec_version, name, created, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, definition_type, definition
